title: Academic review finding
description: One confirmed defect from a review lens. Reports are ARRAYS of these objects, not {"findings": [...]} wrappers. Validate with scripts/validate-findings.py.

id.description: sha1('file:line:locus') — deterministic and LENS-INDEPENDENT, so the same defect found by two different lenses, or rediscovered in a later round, gets the SAME id. Lens is metadata about who found it, not part of what it is.

locus.description: the named thing: a theorem label, table id, function name, slide title, or claim identifier

lens.description: which review lens produced this. Metadata only — NOT part of the finding id, so two lenses finding the same defect dedup to one. Enum extended 2026-08-21 to cover the seven-pass structural lenses; a producer with a genuinely new lens extends the enum in the same commit that introduces the producer.

credibility_question.description: which of the five credibility questions this bears on. Evidence for one never clears another.

rule.description: the specific documented rule or standard violated. A finding that cites no rule is an opinion.

evidence.description: what was actually inspected — a quote, a computed value, a command and its output

failing_case.description: a concrete configuration under which the claim breaks, or the exact missing hypothesis. Not 'this could be clearer'.

mechanical.description: true ONLY for the fixer whitelist (see orchestration-schemas.md). Anything touching an estimand, assumption, specification, or reporting language is NEVER mechanical.

verdict.description: set by the verifier pass; only 'confirmed' findings ship
